judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short payment obligation referring out to the Contract Documents for manner and time.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement's 12.1.3 leaves the application cut-off day and the alternative payment period blank, so the time 'provided in the Contract Documents' is incomplete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Promptly pay each Subcontractor ... reflecting percentages actually retained' is specific though the retention reference is external.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.8 requires at least ten percent retainage on subcontractor payments while Addendum 12.1.7.3 sets five percent on the Fee, so the retention figures come from more than one place.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear negative covenant with a statutory saving.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 9.6.2.1 permits joint payments while disclaiming any obligation to subcontractors, which is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.6.2 and Supplementary Condition 9.6.2.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-acceptance rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.9.3 and 12.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires payments to be 'held' for subcontractors while denying that any trust, fiduciary or tort liability arises — a tension built into one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is conditioned on the absence of a payment bond 'in the full penal sum of the Contract Sum', but Article 16 requires no bond and no Contract Sum figure is stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite trigger periods (seven days) and a stated remedy of stopping Work plus time and cost recovery.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.3's payment dates are blank and Addendum 12.2.2 recasts final payment timing, so the 'date established in the Contract Documents' this remedy depends on is uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sufficiently complete ... so that the Owner can occupy or utilize the Work for its intended use' is the classic evaluative test of substantial completion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 4.4 pays a bonus for early substantial completion and Addendum 4.3 fixes the target date, so the definition carries money with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete listing obligation with an express non-waiver sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.8.3-9.8.5 and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An inspection procedure with a defined re-inspection loop.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.8.1 and 9.8.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It fixes the date and allocates responsibilities and warranty commencement 'unless otherwise provided in the Certificate', which leaves content to a document not yet drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 requires warranties to be assembled at final payment, and Addendum 4.4's bonus turns on the date established here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligation to pay retainage is clear, subject to adjustment for incomplete Work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement's 12.1.7.3 states retainage as 'N/A' while Addendum 12.1.7.3 sets five percent and 12.1.8 sets ten percent for subcontractors, so what retainage is released here is unsettled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short joint-inspection requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.9.3 and 11.4.1.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence non-acceptance rule with an 'unless otherwise agreed' opener.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.6.6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed certification standard qualified by 'to the best of the Architect's knowledge, information and belief'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.3 imposes its own accountants' review and timing and expressly supersedes A201 9.4.1, while Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 adds an Owner acceptance condition to the final Certificate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A five-item list closing with 'other data establishing payment or satisfaction of obligations ... to the extent and in such form as may be designated by the Owner', a general catch-all after specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 12.1.4(b) and 12.2.2 add lien-waiver and title-endorsement requirements, and Article 16 specifies no insurance to be certified under item (2).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Materially delayed' governs entitlement, and the comparison to 'retainage stipulated in the Contract Documents' assumes a stipulated figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No consistent retainage figure exists — 12.1.7.3 says 'N/A', the Addendum says five percent, 12.1.8 says ten percent for subcontractors.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A waiver subject to three enumerated exceptions, which invites an expressio unius argument about anything not listed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 14.6's representations expressly survive final completion, which sits alongside this waiver and may or may not be covered by the exceptions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Waiver on acceptance except for claims 'previously made in writing and identified ... as unsettled' — a precise but easily contested condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4's 30-day arbitration rule operates on the same final-payment moment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, absolute allocation of safety responsibility.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 expressly disclaims Owner responsibility for safety, which reinforces this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable precautions' and 'reasonable protection' are the operative measures, but the three protected categories are itemised.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.18 indemnification and the property insurance provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A compliance obligation in plain terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallels 3.7.2 without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As required by existing conditions and performance of the Contract' plus an illustrative list of safeguards; broad but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 10.1.1 and 10.2.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Utmost care' and 'unusual methods' are unmeasured standards, and the transcription is truncated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Related to 10.3 hazardous materials without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single designation requirement with a default to the superintendent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum Article 2 requires one designated supervisory employee and 3.9.1 requires a competent superintendent, so three provisions name site personnel roles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line prohibition against overloading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger — 'reasonable precautions will be inadequate to prevent foreseeable bodily injury or death' from a material 'including but not limited to asbestos or PCB' — combines a predictive judgment with an open list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 10.3.2 and 10.4's allocation for Contractor-brought materials.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but procedurally specific, with reasonable-objection tests and a defined cost and time remedy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The adjustment is to be 'accomplished as provided in Article 7', which Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 narrows to Change Orders only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the fullest extent permitted by law' with a sole-negligence carve-out; strongly worded but bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors 3.18.1 in the opposite direction and is consistent with 10.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short exception keyed to what the Contract Documents required.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Drawings and Specifications are not enumerated in Article 15, what the Contract Documents 'required' is harder to establish.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At the Contractor's discretion' in an emergency, with compensation determined under 4.3 and Article 7; clear allocation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.7.2 and the Addendum's revision of it restrict emergency cost recovery to costs not caused by the Contractor and not preventable by timely notice, narrowing this route.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eight-item enumeration of insured claims; detailed and closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 16 states no limits of liability, so the coverage this paragraph requires has no specified amount anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not less than limits ... specified in the Contract Documents or required by law, whichever coverage is greater' is a clear formula, provided a figure exists.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 16 is blank and no Supplementary Condition supplies limits, so the primary limb of the formula has no referent — a genuine gap when read with Exhibit E's certificate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Certificates of insurance acceptable to the Owner' and the 30-day cancellation-notice requirement are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit E, the ACORD certificate actually attached, states that the insurer will merely 'endeavor to' give notice and that the certificate confers no rights, which does not satisfy what this paragraph requires.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Owner's usual liability insurance' is entirely undefined — nothing tells the reader what coverage or limits are meant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 16 supplies no limits and Supplementary Condition 11.6 imposes liability for failing to maintain 'insurance required under Article 11', which is hard to apply to an undefined 'usual' policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Optional in nature, with a clear reimbursement rule and a defined minimum limit by cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 3.18.1's indemnity is expressly framed by reference to this optional coverage, so if it was never required the indemnity's opening qualification has no content.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A waiver operating only 'to the extent damages are covered' by an optional policy; the text is also truncated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No such policy is required by Article 16, so the waiver may be inoperative — the same gap that affects 3.18.1 and 11.3.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short prohibition on requiring additional insureds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit E's certificate contemplates an 'additional interest' listing, which sits awkwardly with this prohibition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The required amount is 'the initial Contract Sum plus value of subsequent Contract modifications and cost of materials supplied or installed by others', a formula that depends on a stated Contract Sum.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No initial Contract Sum figure exists — 5.1.1 defines it as Cost of the Work plus Fee and 5.2.1's Guaranteed Maximum Price is 'N/A' — so the insured amount cannot be computed from the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but specific enumeration of covered perils.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 11.4.1.1.1 carves out tools and construction equipment consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear notice-and-substitution mechanism with a cost-shifting rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Change Order route it prescribes is consistent with Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1, though the underlying coverage amount is uncomputable under 11.4.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short allocation sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 11.4.1's 'without optional deductibles' language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short coverage extension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.5.6 and 9.3.2 on off-site storage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional bar on partial occupancy with a cooperation duty; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.9.2 and 9.9.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires only what is 'required in the Contract Documents or by law'; conditional by design.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 16 requires nothing, so the obligation may be empty in this contract.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Optional coverage paired with an absolute waiver of loss-of-use claims 'however caused', which is broad but explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with 4.3.10's consequential damages waiver, pointing the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional waiver keyed to separate Owner policies; detailed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 11.4.7's general waiver of subrogation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete filing and notice obligation on the Owner.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No policy limits are specified in Article 16, so what must be filed is defined only by 11.4.1's uncomputable formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver runs 'to the extent covered by property insurance obtained pursuant to this Paragraph 11.4 or other property insurance applicable to the Work', a coverage-dependent boundary that is frequently litigated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 11.4.1.1.1 requires Contractor equipment policies to carry the same waiver, and 11.6 makes a party liable for failing to maintain required insurance, so the waiver's operation depends on coverage the instrument does not specify.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As their interests may appear' is standard insurance drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 11.4.7 and 9.6.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Work rejected by the Architect or failing to conform' with correction costs 'borne by the Contractor' is categorical, though the transcription is broken.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.7.3 (as revised by the Addendum) makes costs of repairing damaged or nonconforming Work a reimbursable Cost of the Work where not caused by Contractor negligence, which pulls directly against this cost allocation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is truncated mid-clause, so the extension rule it states cannot be applied as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 12.2.2.1 and 12.2.2.3; no conflicting provision was found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As printed it reads 'the one-year period ... shall not be performed by the Contractor', which is missing words and states no intelligible rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its intended effect (no extension by corrective work) is consistent with 12.2.2.2 and 12.2.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense limitation-of-effect provision distinguishing the correction obligation from the limitation period; the transcription is fragmentary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Agreement 12.2.5's post-final-payment correction reimbursement without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The law of the place where the Project is located' is a definite choice given the Hawaii site.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 14.2 uses the same locus for the legal interest rate, and no competing choice-of-law clause appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The transcription drops words in the assignment sentence, leaving the consent requirement and its exception partly unreadable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.3 and A201 5.4.1 both provide for assignment of subcontracts on termination, which are exceptions to this general bar.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only a fragment survives in the text, so no complete rule can be read from it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its cumulative-remedies purpose is consistent with the rest of Article 13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The passage is fragmentary; what remains is a general requirement about tests and approvals with no readable operative sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.4 makes laboratory fees a reimbursable cost except for those relating to defective Work, which is the counterpart of this obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Promptly and, where practicable, at the normal place of testing' is a soft but minor standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.2.2 and 13.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Made promptly to avoid unreasonable delay' is a familiar standard in a one-line provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 13.5 and 8.3.1.
